reviews.title: I really like the H5 Flow and recommend it
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the H5 Flow RGB case for a while now, and it’s definitely a solid choice for anyone looking to build a PC with great airflow and some sleek RGB flair. Here’s what stood out to me: Design & Aesthetics The case looks awesome with its minimalistic design and integrated RGB fans. The RGB lighting is bright but not too over-the-top, and it’s easy to customize using the included software. The tempered glass side panel shows off the internal components really well, making it a nice centerpiece for my setup. Airflow & Cooling Airflow is the standout feature of this case. The mesh front panel and spacious interior allow for great air circulation, which keeps my components cool, even during long gaming sessions. It comes with two pre-installed fans, but there’s room to add more if needed. My RTX 3070 and i5 11400F stay at solid temps without any heat issues, which is exactly what I was hoping for. Before this case my GPU was at 65 idle and 81 gaming now it’s 35 idle and  65-70 gaming Build Quality & Ease of Use The build quality is impressive. The case feels sturdy without being overly heavy. reviews.title: Insane cooling, looks good, good quality.
reviews.comment: I've had this case for about 9 months, got it for an entirely fresh build. I have multiple great things to say, and one complaint. Here's the synopsis: - cooling so good you wouldn't believe it until you have it. - spacious. - no annoying software. - looks great. - tough assemble. Ignore the finger prints in the photo, I refuse to peel off plastic protectors until they're falling off. Cooling. I mostly got this case for looks and price. However, I found out recently that apparently my CPU basically requires liquid cooling. Not with this case, it doesn't. My temps are always cool, everywhere. On that note, I also have an unreasonably large CPU cooler that fits very nicely in there. Looks. It's held up very nicely, no scratches or issues, even after a move. Lights do their own thing, not annoyingly bright, I'm not super invested in that aspect personally. Easily to clean and keep looking nice. All the matierals feel very sturdy, and are very sturdy. Complaint. When I put this thing together I wanted to pull my hair out. It was really frustrating. There are not indicators on the fan directions. They really, really, really need some videos and extra material to help along the process. Very very small thing, the bottom fan needs one of those magnetic wire covers. I lost two screws during the build to that area.
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Inexpensive, easy to build, and cool temps!
reviews.comment: Swapped cases from a smaller Corsair to this H5 Flow and I couldn't be happier. The case looks beautiful and not at all inexpensive. Twin 140mm fans in the front also look great when lit up with ARGB. The side panel definitely is tinted so your computer innards aren't TOO visible, but ARGB definitely shines through. It was a pleasure to build in with the nice removable tray for the front fans and has plenty of room on the back side to hide all of the shameful wires. It looks great and the angled GPU fan light shines through the bottom of the case which gives a nice "underglow" look in the evening. I utilize Fan Control and have custom curves for all of my fans. When web browsing I am able to keep all fans at their minimum speed of ~6XX rpm to keep things quiet and the CPU stays around 30-35C. I never see 100% fan speed on my curves and the temps stay around 70C even with 100% CPU load over an extended time.

reviews.title: Beautiful case. Hassle for an old computer.
reviews.comment: I had some trouble with this case, getting it to work with my old Dell computer. But it's so nice I have to give it four stars. I re-cased my ancient Dell PC's motherboard along with adding a new faster hard drive and more RAM. I was very surprised by the very nice, heavy duty construction and nice styling of the case. The motherboard screwed right in, and my large Nvidia graphics card went in nicely. But the cables that came with it weren't entirely compatible. It seems to be better suited to a newer gaming motherboard. I couldn't get the LED lights to function. I found some YouTube videos and articles showing what I needed. I had to buy two adapter kits and now it works great, except that I can't use the power switch or jacks on the front of the case. I had to mount my old switch on the back of the case. But my kid isn't complaining, he loves it, and now we have a super fast powerful and beautiful gaming PC for a minimal cost.
